title: Mrs. Sweta Dcruz vs Vinod Joseph Sebestian on 5 October, 2026

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT PATNA
 Miscellaneous Appeal No.83 of 2025


 CNR No. BRHC010090932025
======================================================
Mrs. Sweta Dcruz, Wife of Vinod Jaseph Sebestian, Daughter of Navin
Kumar @ N. Deruz, Resident of Ward No-7, Jarahabhatha, Omnagar,
Bilaspur, Municipal, Corporation, Bilaspur, Chattisgarh-495001


 ... ... Appellant/s
 Versus
Vinod Joseph Sebestian, Son of K.J Sebestian Resident of 1/10 New
Patloputra, Colony Church Road, Disrtict-Patna, Bihar


 ... ... Respondent/s
======================================================
Appearance :
For the Appellant/s : Mr. Sagar Suman, Advocate
For the Respondent/s : Mr. Rohitabh Das, Advocate
======================================================
CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BIBEK CHAUDHURI
 and
 HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RANA VIKRAM SINGH
ORAL JUDGMENT
(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE BIBEK CHAUDHURI)


Date: 05-10-2026
 1. The instant matrimonial appeal is directed against

the judgement and decree of dismissal of Matrimonial (Divorce)

Case No. 5313 of 2014, decided by the Additional Principal

Judge, Family Court at Patna under Section 10(1) of the Indian

Christian Marriage Act, 1872.
 2/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




 2. Indisputably, the marriage between the parties were

solemnized on 24th of January, 2010 according to christian rights

and ceremonies in a church at Patliputra Colony, Patna, Bihar.

 3. The applicant / wife was a resident of Bilashpur in

the State of Chhattisgarh. For the purpose of marriage, she

along with her family members had to come to Patna and stay

there for few days before marriage for solemnization of

marriage. It is further contended by the petitioner that the father

of the petitioner paid a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- in the said

marriage to the defendant-husband. Additionally, he paid Rs.

6,00,000/- for purchasing furniture to the defendant. After

marriage, they started to live in the house of the defendant-

husband as husband and wife. There she noticed that one maid

servant, named, Sheela, was all in all in the family of her

husband. Her husband had no other person and the applicant

practically used to spend her days as a maid under the

instructions of the said Sheela. She also noticed unnatural close

relationship of her husband with the said lady. When she

objected, she was abused by her husband, physically assaulted

and subjected to mental cruelty. On 10th of March, 2010, failing

to bear such torture, the applicant went to her paternal house at

Bilashpur. The defendant-husband came Bilashpur on 14th of
 3/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




March, 2010 and tried to take her back to Patna but she refused

to come. It is contended by the applicant-wife that her husband

is a man of means. He deals with the surgical items at Ashok

Rajpath, Patna. He earns Rs. 3,00,000/- per month at the

relevant point of time. Apart from the said income, he has huge

landed property. On the other hand, the applicant is a housewife

having no source of income.

 4. The respondent filed a written statement, denying

all allegations made out in the plaint by the applicant. He

specifically denied any illicit relationship with any lady. He also

denied the allegation of cruelty and also the allegation of having

huge amount of income. On the other hand, he submits that he

carries on his life as philanthropist, imparting education to 25-

30 poor children.

 5. On the basis of the pleadings, the learned Trial

Judge framed as many as five issues and finally came to the

conclusion that the applicant failed to prove her case and she is

not entitled to get any decree of divorce.

 6. We are surprised to note that the learned Trial Judge

considered the case under Section 10(1) of the Christian

Marriage Act, 1872. The said Act does not govern dissolution of

marriage for christian couples in India. The Divorce Act, 1869 is
 4/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




the governing Act for divorce for christian couples in India. It

deals with the dissolution of marriage between a man and the

woman in the christian community. It is a codified Indian

Personal Law. It states that when either the husband or the wife

files a petition for divorce, the Court of Law grants separation in

accordance with the provisions of the Act. The provisions of the

Act deals with various rights after divorce which include

grounds for dissolution of marriage, custody of child, alimony,

distribution of property visiting the child and likewise.

 7. It is unfortunate to note that a Judicial Officer in the

rank of Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at Patna

passed an order in a suit without even verifying the Statute

applicable to adjudicate the lis. It is not only an ignorance, but

sheer negligence on the part of the concerned Trial Judge. If this

happens, we are afraid about the future of judiciary in the State

of Bihar.

 8. Be that as it may, marriage of the parties were

solemnized on 24th of January, 2010. From the materials on

record, it is ascertained that the appellant left her matrimonial

home on 10th of March, 2010.

 9. It is contended by the husband respondent that after

marriage, the appellant used to pick up quarrel with him on
 5/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




small household matters. The respondent had a maid servant,

who used to work in the house of the respondent from before his

marriage. The appellant alleged that the respondent had illicit

relationship with the maid servant. The said maid servant was

examined on behalf of the respondent. She said in her

deposition that she had been working for about 20-25 years in

the house of the respondent. She used to stay in the same house.

She did not know the reason for dispute between the parties.

 10. The appellant, on the other hand, deposed that the

said maid servant was practically all in all in the family of her

husband. She also alleged that her husband had illicit

relationship with the said lady and when she protested, her

husband assaulted her physically.

 11. On perusal of the lower court records, especially

the deposition of the parties, we find that the appellant failed to

prove the allegation of adultery. However, there shall be no

order as to costs. It is amply proved that the appellant has

deserted her husband since 2010 and the matrimonial case was

filed in the year 2014. Thus, the appellant has deserted the

respondent for more than two years immediately before

presentation of plaint. On the ground of desertion, the appellant

is entitled to get a decree of dissolution of marriage by divorce.
 6/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




 12. In view of the above discussion, we have no other

alternative but to set aside the judgement passed by the Trial

Court. Accordingly, the judgement and decree of dismissal of

Matrimonial (Divorce) Case No. 5313 of 2014, decided by the

Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at Patna under Section

10(1) of the Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872, is set aside.

 13. The instant appeal is allowed.

 14. The appellant do get a decree for divorce against

her husband, namely Vinod Joseph Sebestian from the date of

delivery of this judgement. Marital tie between the parties is

also dissolved.

 15. Now comes the question of permanent alimony. It

has already been recorded that the appellant did not come

forward to contest the instant appeal. However, the appellant

filed affidavit of assets and liabilities on 10th of December,

2025. It is found from the said affidavit that on the date of filing

of the affidavit, the appellant was 40 years of age. In paragraph

17 of the affidavit, she has stated that she is dependent upon her

paternal home. In paragraph no. 22, she has stated that she was

granted maintenance at the rate of Rs. 10,000/- per month vide

order, dated 23rd of December, 2019, passed in MJC No. 180 of

2019 by the Additional Principal Judge, Family Court at
 7/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




Bilashpur and the respondent has refused and neglected to pay

maintenance amount since February, 2025. It is also stated in the

affidavit of assets and liabilities that the respondent husband has

an X-ray Clinic and a shop for surgical items, situated at Ashok

Rajpath, Patna. He has a Doctors Clinic. He is the owner of St.

Sebastian School. He also runs a business of real estate. He is a

practicing Advocate of Patna High Court and a Marketing

Consultant. He has his own house at Patlaputra Colony, Patna,

one of the most sophisticated locality of the city. The appellant

also stated that respondent does not have any liability. The

appellant states her total liability per month at the rate of

40450/-

 16. The respondent has also filed his assets and

liabilities. It is stated by him that as per income tax return, his

total income for the assessment year 2025-26 is 1,73,740/- and

his rental income is 2,48,000/-, total being Rs. 4,21,740/-. As

there was gulp of difference between the claim of the contesting

parties with regard to assets and liabilities, we decided to

appoint a Special Officer to find out the extent of property

owned by the respondent. The Special Officer submitted his

report on 30th of September, 2026. It is pertinent to reproduce

the report of the said Special Officer hereinbelow: -

 "IN THE HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT

 17.09.2026

whereby the Hon'ble Court directed

(i) X-Ray & Surgical, opposite Women Hospital,

(ii) -- Doctor's Clinic;

(iv) Advocate, Patna High Court;

X-Ray & Surgical

2. That in compliance of the directions passed by the

 and local persons, I located the shop and found the shop to be

3. That upon enquiry from the local persons and other
 shopkeepers, it was found that the shop is not functional from
 last 2-3 years. I was informed that after the death of father of
 Respondent, a medicine shop "Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushidhi
 Kendra" was opened which was also closed shortly after

4. That I visited the shop at different times on different
 days to ascertain if shop opens anytime of the day, however,
 the shop was found closed all the time.

Photographs of shop are
 attached as Annexure 1 for kind perusal

 Doctor's Clinic

5. Upon enquiry, it was found that no doctor's clinic is

Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




 functional either in the house of the Respondent or in the
 shop situated in Ashok Rajpath, Patna.
St. Sebastian School

6. Upon enquiry from neighbours of the Respondent, it
 was found that a St. Sebastian School was running from the
 house of the Respondent, however, the same is not functional
 since last 3-4 years.

7. No sign board / nameplate of St. Sebastian School
 was found on the house of Respondent.
Advocate, Patna High Court

8. I looked for filings for last three years against the
 AUIN of Respondent i.e. 104649 and I found one case filed
 against the AUIN of the Respondent vide TEST
 CASE-18360/2025 filed on 31.07.2025 and the same

Case status of TEST CASE-18360 /

 Real _Estate Management _and__ Marketing
 Consultant.

9. I made a discreet enquiry from the neighbours of the
 Respondent in New Patliputra Colony, Patna and it was found
 that Respondent is not engaged in such business of Real
 Estate or Marketing Consultant.
Property owned by the Respondent

10. Petitioner is the owner of the plot admeasuring 2 | Katha
 13 Dhur 6.4 Dhurki (8.36 Decimal) (3630 Sq | Ft) situated at

Photographs of house are attached as

12. Upon visiting the house of Respondent on

13. Upon query, though the Respondent admitted the

14. Upon searching the records from Patna Municipal

Property details from Patna

15. Upon discreet enquiry from the neighbours, I found

17. Upon searching for the details of property of the
 Respondent, it was found that Respondent has mortgaged his

 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026

 with Yes Bank Ltd. vide Registered Mortgage Deed No. 21219

 Copy of Mortgage Deed is attached

18. From perusal of the registered mortgage deed, it is

 "M/s Aryabhat Tecnotrader Pvt. Ltd." having

 Crores wherein three properties and fixed

19. Among, three properties kept as collateral by Yes
 Bank Ltd., one property belongs to the Respondent.

20. Value of the property as declared by the Yes Bank
 Ltd. in the mortgage deed is Rs. 4 Crores.

21. M/s Aryabhat Tecnotrader Pvt. Ltd. is engaged in
 construction related works and has participated in different

22. Two writ petitions (CWJC No. 3551 /2025 and CWJC
 No. 3557 / 2025) filed by M/s Aryabhat Tecnotrader Pvt. Ltd.
 were found pending in Hon'ble Patna High Court.

Prepared and submitted by
 Dhananjay Kashyap
 AUIN- 101879
 Ph-8690054511"

17. As per the income tax return and rental income,

the total income of the respondent is Rs. 4,21,740/-. The Special

Officer's report discloses another income of Rs. 15,000/- per

month, i.e., 1,80,000/- per annum from the rent receipt by the

respondent from Logos Christian Books and Music Centre. The

respondent has residential house of 2 Katha, 13 Dhur and 6.4

Dhurki (8.36 Decimal) (4630 Ft.). He mortgaged his property
 12/13
 Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026




and fixed deposits of Rs. 1.5 crore to obtain commercial loan for

a sum of Rs. 9.80 crores for Ms. Aryabhat Technotrader Pvt.

Ltd. The said company deals with real estate business. Value of

the mortgaged property was declared by Yes Bank Limited as

Rs. 4 crores.

18. Thus, beside the above declared income and rental

income, the respondent is the owner of property worth Rs. 4

crores. Therefore, the respondent is a man of substance. The

appellant stated her monthly expenditure at Rs. 40,450/-. In

order to have the said amount, the appellant needs at least

permanent alimony of Rs. 50,00,000/- and if the said amount is

kept in fixed deposit, she may earn Rs. 40,000/- per month and

maintain her livelihood.

19. In view of such circumstances and for the reasons

stated above, we are of the considered view that the respondent

is under obligation to pay a sum of Rs. 50,00,000/- to the

appellant towards permanent alimony. Such amount shall be

paid within a period of three months from the date of this order.

On payment of such amount, the respondent does not require to

pay the maintenance allowance. On payment of permanent

alimony, any case pending between the parties, arising out of

matrimonial relation shall be dropped by the concerned courts.
 13/13
Patna High Court MA No. 83 of 2025 dt.05-10-2026

20. With the above order, the instant appeal is

 disposed of.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J)
